claims.claim_vi: An analyzer is made of character filters, a tokenizer and token filters, applied in order.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment's term vectors of 'Bộ nhớ đệm giữ dữ liệu hay dùng' gave eight terms with positions 0 to 7.

claims.claim_vi: Lucene indexes are made of segments, each a fully independent index; indexes evolve by creating new segments and merging existing ones; deleted documents are dropped when segments are merged.
claims.verified_by: Read the 10.5.1 source; the experiment showed three segments after three refreshes, an update marking the old copy deleted in _0 and adding _3, and a force merge producing one segment _4.

claims.claim_vi: The .tim file is the term dictionary with per-term statistics and pointers into .doc and .pos; the .tip file is an index into the term dictionary for random access.
claims.section: Term Dictionary; Term Index; file extensions table
claims.verified_by: Read; the merged shard directory held _4_Lucene104_0.tim, .tip, .doc and .pos with index.compound_format false.

claims.claim_vi: A refresh writes and opens a new segment so documents become searchable without a full commit; indices refresh every second by default when searched in the last 30 seconds.

An index is one or more primary shards, each a self-contained Lucene index; replicas copy primaries for fault tolerance and read capacity; primary count is fixed at creation, replica count can change.
Elasticsearch never assigns a replica to the same node as its primary; a single-node cluster with replicas is always yellow.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment's index with one replica reported yellow with 1 unassigned shard.

claims.claim_vi: Updates are an atomic delete of the old document plus indexing of the new one; soft deletes keep recent deletions for replay, held by shard history retention leases that expire after 12h by default.
claims.verified_by: Read; right after the force merge the experiment still counted 1 deleted document. Why it was kept at that moment was not traced.

claims.claim_vi: In most cases the same analyzer should be used at index and search time; the term query should not be used on text fields because their values are analyzed.
claims.section: Index and search analysis; Avoid using the term query for text fields

design_notes_vi: Bốn bước đánh số theo đường đi của tài liệu, bốn ghi chú kết quả thử. Không đặt tên tệp .tim, .tip vào chữ của hình. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source says Elasticsearch builds the term dictionary using an LSM tree; per the Lucene source the LSM-like part is writing immutable segments and merging them, while the term dictionary inside a segment is a sorted file (.tim) with an index (.tip).
Source lists features and use cases; the lesson follows one document through analyzer, inverted index, segments and shards, each checked in an experiment.
Source says schema-free JSON documents; the lesson leaves that out and points to mappings (text versus keyword) as a learning step, since the type of a field decides how it is searched.
